newsitem.title: INDIA: Strong rupee may have slowed India exports - RBI.
newsitem.headline: Strong rupee may have slowed India exports - RBI.

text.p: India's strengthening rupee could have played a role in the recent deceleration of its export growth, an official of the country's central bank told Reuters Financial Television on Friday.

"Exports have lost a bit of their dynamism," Deputy Governor Y.V. Reddy of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), said in an interview. "There are both external and internal reasons, some protectionist measures outside. But internally also there have been environmental constraints."
Global investment bank Merrill Lynch said in a recent India report that the strong rupee was hurting Indian exports.

"Exports grew at only four percent in FY 1996/97 (April-March) against an 18 percent average growth rate for the previous three years," Merrill's report said. "The real appreciation of the rupee is having a negative impact on exports."
Reddy said: "But it is also true that the exchange rate could have -- the strong rupee could have -- played a role in this slight deceleration."
The rupee has remained steady at 35.70/80 against the dollar for the past one year.
